chunks: From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about a man who passes by carrion in the water. He said: "He performs wudu (ablution) from the side in which there is no carrion."

key_terms.النَّاحِيَةِ: the side or direction of the water source
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: water, the substance being considered for purification
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion; a dead animal carcass found in the water
key_terms.لَيْسَ فِيهَا: in which it is not present, indicating separation from contamination
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution) for ritual purification

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing wudu (ablution) from water that contains a carcass?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water in which a dead carcass is present. It indicates that one may perform wudu (ablution) from the side of the water not containing the carcass, showing practical guidance on taharah and the use of water.
